findings.title: addMembers/removeMember actions swallow errors silently
findings.body: The `addMembers` action (line 61-65) calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and `removeMember` (line 51-59) calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` without attaching a `.catch`/error handler on the returned promise, unlike `save` and `destroy` which do handle rejection with `bootbox.alert`. The backend (`Admin::GroupsController#add_members`/`#remove_member`) returns a 422 with an error message when the group is automatic, or can fail for other reasons (e.g. unknown usernames silently skipped, group save validation failure). Because there is no error handler, any such failure is silently swallowed in the UI and the user gets no feedback that the add/remove operation did not succeed.

findings.title: `automatic` lookup in item view template resolves against the member, not the group
findings.body: `group_member.hbs` is rendered as the template for the `group-member` itemView used via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` in `group.hbs`. Since this is the non-block `{{each}}` form with an `itemView`, the rendering context for each item's template is the member object itself, not the outer group/controller context. The bare `{{#unless automatic}}` check in this template therefore resolves `automatic` against the `member` (a user object, which has no `automatic` property) rather than against the group's `automatic` flag, so it will always be falsy and the remove link will be rendered for members of automatic groups too, even though removal is disallowed server-side. This produces a UI affordance that always fails (compounded by the missing error handling noted elsewhere), misleading admins into thinking they can remove members from automatic groups.

findings.title: Membership mutation is persisted before validation/save, causing misleading error responses
findings.body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` (line 90) immediately executes a DELETE against the join table for a persisted `group`/association, and in `add_members`, `group.add(user)` (line 73) similarly persists membership immediately via the association. Only afterwards is `group.save` called to determine the HTTP response. If `group.save` fails for any unrelated reason (e.g. stale validation state), the controller renders `render_json_error(group)` even though the membership change has already been committed to the database. Clients receiving an error response will believe the operation failed and may retry, potentially causing duplicate adds or confusing inconsistent state, since the actual membership mutation already succeeded independent of the `save` result.

findings.title: Unhandled RecordNotFound possible when removing a non-member/invalid user_id
findings.body: `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer id and no rescue. Depending on how the has_many association's `delete` resolves an id that is not currently part of the group's collection (e.g. stale client state, concurrent removal, or a malicious/incorrect user_id), this can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is not rescued here and would bubble up as an unhandled 500 error instead of a clean validation error response. There is also no spec covering this scenario (see spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb), so this regression path is untested.

findings.title: Default member page size silently reduced for automatic groups
findings.body: The previous implementation gave automatic groups a larger default limit (200) specifically to work around truncation for groups with many members, while non-automatic groups were unpaginated/unlimited. The new code applies a flat default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` to all groups regardless of the `automatic` flag. This is a behavior change for the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint: large automatic groups (e.g. trust-level groups) that used to return up to 200 members by default now only return 50, which can break any existing API consumers or UI relying on the previous default page size, without any changelog/doc update reflecting this change.

findings.title: Misleading singular placeholder text for a multi-username input
findings.body: `admin.groups.selector_placeholder` was changed from "add users" to "enter username" (singular). However, the `user-selector` field it labels (used in `admin/templates/group.hbs`) accepts a comma-separated list of usernames that are split and processed as multiple users in `addMembers`/`Admin::GroupsController#add_members`. The new singular wording suggests only one username can be entered, which is misleading to admins trying to add multiple members at once.

findings.title: Usernames input is not cleared after successfully adding members
findings.body: The `addMembers` action contains a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment acknowledging that `this.get("usernames")` is never reset after a successful add. This means the previously entered usernames remain in the input field after the members are added, and clicking "Add" again (or forgetting the field still has old content) will re-submit the same usernames, causing redundant/no-op requests and a confusing UX for admins managing group membership.
